subject: S3 access anomaly: evidence and SOC 2 / SIG packaging
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Amira Rahman <amira@healthcore.com>, security@healthcore.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: S3 access anomaly: initial notify + immediate evidence ask

Team / Amira,

We detected an anomalous pattern of GET requests against one of HealthCore's S3 prefixes in the eu-west-1 replica bucket at ~2026-11-20T23:04:12Z. The traffic was identified by our telemetry pipeline (prefix-fingerprint rule) as coming from a long-lived service key that had recently been used from an IP range not previously observed for that key.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Rotated the implicated service key and revoked active sessions tied to it (rotation timestamp: 2026-11-20T23:18:05Z).
- Applied an emergency bucket policy to deny non-owner principal reads on the affected prefix.
- Snapshot exported CloudTrail events and S3 object access logs for the 24-hour window centered on the anomaly.
- Throttled any suspect inbound requests while preserving forensics copies.

What we need from HealthCore / for SOC 2 & SIG packaging (requested ASAP):
1) Confirmation of whether the affected keys are owned by an external integration (name/email) or a HealthCore service account.
2) Confirmation of the data classifications for objects under the affected prefix (PII / PHI / tokenized / internal).
3) Any downstream systems that read from that prefix (ETL jobs, replication targets).

I will prepare a formal evidence bundle for SOC 2 / SIG review containing: CloudTrail filtered export, S3 access manifest, redaction map, and a short IR summary. Jonas / Marissa — please coordinate redaction and produce the initial bundle for review.

Attachments (incoming): s3_access_manifest_20261120.csv (stub), cloudtrail_filtered_20261120.json.gz (stub).

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

--
On Sat, 21 Nov 2026 at 08:40 Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — I’m on it.
>
> Quick questions for handoff to forensics:
> - Do we want a full object-level access dump (object keys + byte counts) or a manifest (key list + access timestamps)? Full dumps can be heavy; manifest is usually sufficient for SIG/SOC reviews.
> - Any constraints from HealthCore on redaction (hashing vs truncation)?
>
> I’ll pull the CloudTrail filtered export, the S3 server access logs for the replica, and the IAM change timeline. Will deliver as encrypted artifacts to the Drive folder and paste the link here.
>
> Jonas
> Security Operations Lead
> jonas@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, CrowdSecure Forensics <forensics@crowdsecure.io>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: S3 access anomaly: initial notify + immediate evidence ask

Sofia / Marissa,

Uploading artifacts now. Plan:
- cloudtrail_filtered_20261120.json.gz (CloudTrail events filtered to HealthCore ARNs + implicated access key)
- s3_access_manifest_20261120.csv (object key, timestamp, requester, operation, byte_count)
- iam_key_timeline_20261120.csv (last rotated, owner principal)

CrowdSecure: please start a forensic image of any ephemeral compute that was used by the implicated principal (we see a cross-region hop in IPs). Use the SEC-427 Jira to track chain-of-custody.

Note on redaction: default approach will be to hash object keys and truncate any object bodies. We’ll produce a redaction_map_20261122.csv that maps hashed_key -> original_key for in-house review; HealthCore will get the hashed keys in the public evidence bundle unless you request otherwise.

Deliverables (ETA): initial encrypted bundle to Drive by 2026-11-21T12:00-08:00.

Jonas

--
On Sat, 21 Nov 2026 at 09:05 Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com> wrote:
> Noted and thank you.
>
> Amira / HealthCore: we will avoid including raw object contents in the shared SOC 2/SIG packet unless explicitly requested. We’ll include object-level metadata and timestamped access events. If you confirm the objects contain regulated data (PHI), we will escalate the redaction to replace keys with truncated tokens and provide an additional auditor-only bundle under NDA.
>
> S

From: Amira Rahman <amira@healthcore.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthcore.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: S3 access anomaly: initial notify + immediate evidence ask

Sofia / Jonas,

Thanks for the rapid notification and for the immediate mitigation steps. A few notes from HealthCore side: we are confirming ownership of the implicated service key; initial internal mapping shows the prefix stores de-identified telemetry and a small set of patient metadata (hashed IDs). That said, we treat the prefix as sensitive by policy.

Items we need from Redwood to satisfy our internal SOC 2 desk review and to pass our vendor SIG: 
- Canonical CloudTrail export for the 48-hour window (we may ask for additional days after initial review).
- Filtered S3 access manifest with requester ARN, IP, and user-agent.
- Chain-of-custody and who on Redwood received the evidence.
- Confirmation that any object content shared will be hashed and that original object content is not shared publicly.

We also need an initial post-incident summary outlining root cause hypotheses, steps taken, and remediation timeline (suitable for our InfoSec leadership). Please advise when the sanitized packet is available and we’ll coordinate with our legal/compliance.

— Amira Rahman
Director, Security Operations, HealthCore
amira@healthcore.com
security@healthcore.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Amira Rahman <amira@healthcore.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, CrowdSecure Forensics <forensics@crowdsecure.io>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: S3 access anomaly: evidence bundle and short postmortem (attached)

Amira / Team,

Attached is the sanitized evidence bundle we discussed and a short postmortem. Deliverables:
- ir_postmortem_summary_20261122.pdf (summary for HealthCore InfoSec, includes timeline and root-cause analysis)
- cloudtrail_filtered_20261120.json.gz (events filtered to implicated key + full requester metadata)
- s3_access_manifest_20261120.csv (object key hashes, access timestamps, requester_arn, ip, user_agent)
- redaction_map_20261122.csv (internal; will be shared under NDA if requested)
- evidence_readme_20261122.txt (instructions for reviewers; contact points and chain-of-custody notes)

Executive summary (short):
- Timeline: initial anomalous reads observed 2026-11-20T23:04:12Z; containment applied 2026-11-20T23:18:05Z; initial artifacts exported 2026-11-21T12:00-08:00.
- Root cause (conclusion so far): compromised long-lived service key used from an unusual origin; likely the key was exfiltrated from a third-party CI job configured with broad read permissions. We are investigating the CI account as the next step.
- Remediation: forced rotation of implicated key, tightened bucket policy to deny cross-account reads, applied least-privilege guardrails on replication keys, and an account-level review of long-lived credentials.

Next steps:
1) HealthCore to confirm whether you need the redaction_map under NDA for internal mapping.
2) If you want expanded CloudTrail for 7 days, respond and we will schedule the export (may add 2–4 hours).
3) We will add a short SLA note to SEC-427 with expected timelines for any required auditor-only artifacts.

Drive link (encrypted folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqT3-ExampleDriveLink
Jira for tracking: SEC-427 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-427)

Attachments included in bundle: ir_postmortem_summary_20261122.pdf, cloudtrail_filtered_20261120.json.gz, s3_access_manifest_20261120.csv, redaction_map_20261122.csv, evidence_readme_20261122.txt

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

--
Note: If HealthCore legal requests a signed NDA to receive the redaction_map, please loop in Priya Natarajan (privacy) and we’ll expedite.
